dedupe_keys.name: material stock maps of buildings and mobility infrastructure at 10 m austria germany contiguous us uk and ireland

description: This series maps the mass of materials stocked in buildings and mobility infrastructure on a 10-metre grid, from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Earth observation, OpenStreetMap and material intensity factors. It comes from the group of Helmut Haberl and Dominik Wiedenhofer at BOKU University Vienna's Institute of Social Ecology with David Frantz and Franz Schug (Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, later Trier University and the University of Wisconsin) and partners, published on Zenodo: Austria (8 February 2021) and Germany (11 February 2021), representative of about 2018; the contiguous United States (version 1.1, July 2023) with regional parts and the 3D building and infrastructure layers behind it (September 2022); and the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland (29 July 2024). Layers give area and mass by building type and street type and by material. The UK and Ireland stocks total 19.8 gigatonnes, or 279 tonnes per person, mostly aggregate, concrete and bricks. Coverage: the five countries named. Access: tiled GeoTIFFs with a VRT mosaic; the US and German archives are about 22 and 78 GB. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: estimates rest on material intensity factors and building heights derived from satellites. Simulation uses: circular economy, embodied carbon and reconstruction mass for disaster scenarios. Related records: the Finnish residential material inventory.
